## Load packages

```{r setup}
pacman::p_load(here, limma, writexl)
here::i_am("02_Differential_Expression/01_Design/a_script/01_design.qmd")
```

## Read sample metadata

The design uses the metadata attached to the protein matrix, so it follows the same sample order.
The table counts samples per treatment and timepoint.

```{r read}
proteins <- readRDS(here("01_Preprocess", "02_Quantification", "c_data", "proteins.rds"))
targets <- proteins$targets

with(targets, table(treatment, timepoint))
```

## Design

A design matrix has one row per sample and one column per model coefficient, marking which group
and participant each sample belongs to. `~ 0 + group + participant` gives one mean per
treatment-by-timepoint group, no separate intercept, and a fixed effect per participant. Participant
is fixed rather than random because every contrast sits within one person (limma User's Guide
§9.4.2), which makes pre-to-post comparisons paired. A participant-level variable such as sex is
constant within person and cannot be estimated here.

`makeContrasts()` reads its arguments as R code, so a column named `groupBFR_T1` must become
`BFR_T1` and every name must be syntactic. `is.fullrank()` checks that the columns are linearly
independent; a rank-deficient design would leave contrasts inestimable.

```{r design}
design <- model.matrix(~ 0 + group + participant, data = targets)
colnames(design) <- sub("^group", "", colnames(design))
rownames(design) <- targets$sample_id

stopifnot(
  is.fullrank(design),
  identical(make.names(colnames(design)), colnames(design))
)

c(
  samples = nrow(design), coefficients = ncol(design),
  residual_df = nrow(design) - ncol(design)
)
```

## Check within-leg correlation

Samples from the same leg may stay correlated after the participant term. `leg_id` marks each
participant and leg; `duplicateCorrelation()` takes the protein matrix, the design and that block,
and returns the average residual correlation within legs.

```{r correlation-strata}
leg_id <- paste(targets$participant, targets$leg, sep = "_")

strata <- data.frame(
  level = "within leg, participant fixed (unweighted matrix correlation)",
  correlation = duplicateCorrelation(proteins$E, design, block = leg_id)$consensus.correlation
)
round(strata$correlation, 3)
```

The estimate ignores the standard errors and sample weights the later fit uses, and a small value
does not prove there is no dependence. `02_Differential` fits without a leg block while this stays
near zero. If it rose, the fix is `block = leg_id` there; `leg_id` is not saved, so read this value
on every rerun.

## Contrasts

A contrast is a difference between model coefficients; positive values follow the subtraction
order below. `makeContrasts()` returns one column of coefficient weights per comparison.

```{r contrasts}
contrast_matrix <- makeContrasts(
  `BFR_Post-Pre` = BFR_T2 - BFR_T1,
  `HLRT_Post-Pre` = HLRT_T2 - HLRT_T1,
  `BFR_Pre-HLRT_Pre` = BFR_T1 - HLRT_T1,
  `BFR_Post-HLRT_Post` = BFR_T2 - HLRT_T2,
  Modality_x_Time_Interaction = (BFR_T2 - BFR_T1) - (HLRT_T2 - HLRT_T1),
  levels = design
)
contrast_matrix[rowSums(abs(contrast_matrix)) > 0, ]
```

| Name | Role | Compares | Reads as |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Modality_x_Time_Interaction` | primary | difference of the two time effects | the study question |
| `BFR_Pre-HLRT_Pre` | baseline | two legs before training | baseline leg difference |
| `BFR_Post-Pre` | secondary, exploratory | one leg over time | what restricted training did |
| `HLRT_Post-Pre` | secondary, exploratory | the other leg over time | what conventional training did |
| `BFR_Post-HLRT_Post` | secondary, exploratory | two legs after training | leg difference at the end |

`Modality_x_Time_Interaction` equals `BFR_Post-HLRT_Post` minus `BFR_Pre-HLRT_Pre` exactly, so the
five are not independent questions. The interaction tests whether the change over time differs
between treatments. Baseline differences can exist and are inspected, not assumed absent.

## Save results

`design.rds` holds the design, the contrasts and the name of the baseline contrast for the models
downstream. `01_design.xlsx` holds an overview, the samples, the design, the contrasts and the
correlation check; identifier columns keep the matrix row names in Excel.

```{r write}
out <- here("02_Differential_Expression", "01_Design", "c_data")
saveRDS(
  list(design = design, contrasts = contrast_matrix, baseline = "BFR_Pre-HLRT_Pre"),
  file.path(out, "design.rds")
)
sheets <- list(
  samples = as.data.frame(targets),
  design = data.frame(sample_id = rownames(design), design, check.names = FALSE),
  contrasts = data.frame(
    coefficient = rownames(contrast_matrix), contrast_matrix, check.names = FALSE
  ),
  correlation_strata = strata
)
overview <- data.frame(
  sheet = names(sheets), rows = sapply(sheets, nrow), columns = sapply(sheets, ncol),
  description = c(
    "Sample identifiers and study metadata",
    "Design matrix, one row per sample",
    "Contrast weights, one column per comparison",
    "Within-leg correlation, participant fixed"
  )
)
write_xlsx(c(list(overview = overview), sheets), file.path(out, "01_design.xlsx"))
```
